name: Conveyor
intent: Arrows at both ends of a row or column that is too long to fit, so people can move it along without a scrollbar.
usage: Use Conveyor around a run of pieces that does not fit, like eight scorecards in a Scoreboard, a row of filter chips or a tall side list. It is one component: put the run inside it. The arrows show only when there is something to scroll, and each one turns off at its end. A soft fade sits where the content passes under an arrow. A press moves most of a screenful, or the step you set. The row can also be scrolled by hand, with a trackpad, or with the arrow keys when it has focus. Put a Scoreboard inside it with scroll off, so the Conveyor does the scrolling. For paged slides with a Slide 2 of 5 caption, use Carousel. See contracts/conveyor.json for the full contract.

children.note: The run that scrolls, like a Scoreboard or a row of chips.

orientation.note: Horizontal puts the arrows left and right. Vertical puts them above and below, and needs a height on the Conveyor.

step.note: Pixels one press moves. Without it, a press moves 80% of what is in view.

label.note: What is scrolling, like Key metrics. It names the row for screen readers and reads in the arrows, like Scroll key metrics right.

useWhen: More than five or six scorecards in a Scoreboard.
A row of chips, cards or tabs that runs past the edge.
A tall list in a narrow column, scrolled up and down.
doNot: Do not use it for paged slides or a gallery. Use Carousel.
Do not use it to page a table. Use Pagination.
Do not put a second scrolling box inside it; turn that one's scrolling off.
Do not hide the only way to reach content behind the arrows alone; the row still scrolls by hand and by keyboard.
a11y: The run is a group with the label, and a focus stop, so the arrow keys scroll it.
Each arrow is a kit Button that says what it does, like Scroll key metrics right.
An arrow turns off at its end of the run.
Smooth scrolling is off when the person prefers reduced motion.

examples.title: A row that does not fit
examples.usage: The arrows show only when there is something to scroll, and turn off at the ends.
